A+B HYBRID — built from your lean (Aug 29)
A's three action rows stay always-open with their prompts and live counts. Everything below consolidates into four doors (B) that expand IN PLACE — accordion, not new hub screens — so collapsed, the whole page fits one screen with zero scrolling. 'Teddy's records' is shown expanded.
One section open at a time; the app remembers your last-open door.

THE PROBLEM (your feedback, Aug 28)
26 identical tiles, flat grid: no hierarchy (Letters = Blog), no grouping (one workflow scattered across three rows), labels without meaning ("Your Result"), and 26 choices at once for someone who is already exhausted.

Shared by all three concepts: group by job-to-be-done, 44px+ targets, "Everything else" collapsed so nothing is lost, and the Quick Actions row is dropped (it duplicates the tab bar exactly).

A · FRONT POCKET — recommended
List rows with one-line plain-language descriptions: the row teaches the app while you scan. Live counts (2 running · 1 reply) where they exist. Search on top.
Tradeoff: longer page; fewer items per screen than a grid.

B · FIVE DOORS
Five hub cards, five choices, the calmest Home; the workhorse hub is full-width with live counts. Bottom of the artboard shows what a hub opens into.
Tradeoff: every tool is one extra tap away; hub screens are new surfaces to build.

C · SHORTCUTS FIRST
Four personalized shortcut tiles (learned from usage, sensible defaults first), then compact grouped rows.
Tradeoff: compact rows lose the teaching descriptions; personalization needs a small usage-tracking increment.

AFTER YOUR PICK
1 · toolsCatalog.ts — every destination with group, label, description, route (trilingual, tested)
2 · HomeScreen swap (Ionicons stay; these SVGs map 1:1)
3 · "Everything else" screen — A-Z, searchable, so all 26 destinations stay reachable
4 · If C: AsyncStorage tap-counts pick the shortcut four.

Mix-and-match is fine — e.g. A's action section with C's shortcuts row on top.
